title: How comic books can help you learn - Gene Luen Yang
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】漫畫書如何幫助你學習 - Gene Luen Yang（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: When I was in the fifth grade, I bought an issue of DC Comics Presents number 57
cues.en: When I was in the fifth grade, I bought an issue of DC Comics Presents number 57
cues.zh: 五年級的時候，我從我家附近 書店的旋轉書架上買了一本

cues.text: off of a spinner rack at my local bookstore.
cues.en: off of a spinner rack at my local bookstore.
cues.zh: 第五十七集的《DC 漫畫特刊》。

cues.text: And that comic book changed my life.
cues.en: And that comic book changed my life.
cues.zh: 那本漫畫改變了我的人生。

cues.text: I immediately fell in love with the medium of comics.
cues.en: I immediately fell in love with the medium of comics.
cues.zh: 我馬上就愛上了漫畫這種媒介。

cues.text: But I never brought them to school.
cues.en: But I never brought them to school.
cues.zh: 但我從來不會帶漫畫 去學校，因為我直覺知道

cues.text: Instinctively, I knew that comic books didn’t belong in the classroom.
cues.en: Instinctively, I knew that comic books didn’t belong in the classroom.
cues.zh: 但我從來不會帶漫畫 去學校，因為我直覺知道 漫畫不該出現在教室裡。

cues.text: Eventually, I became a published cartoonist, writing and drawing comic books for a living.
cues.en: Eventually, I became a published cartoonist, writing and drawing comic books for a living.
cues.zh: 最終，我成了有出版作品的漫畫家， 靠撰寫和繪製漫畫來維生。

cues.text: I also became a high school teacher.
cues.en: I also became a high school teacher.
cues.zh: 我也成了高中老師。

cues.text: This is where I taught: Bishop O’Dowd High School in Oakland, California.
cues.en: This is where I taught: Bishop O’Dowd High School in Oakland, California.
cues.zh: 我教書的地方是加州 奧克蘭的奧多德主教高中。

cues.text: I remember telling my students on the first day of every class that I was also a cartoonist.
cues.en: I remember telling my students on the first day of every class that I was also a cartoonist.
cues.zh: 我記得在每門課的第一堂課 我都會告訴我的學生我身兼漫畫家。

cues.text: I was hoping comics would make them think that I was cool.
cues.en: I was hoping comics would make them think that I was cool.
cues.zh: 我希望漫畫會讓他們覺得我很酷。

cues.text: I was wrong.
cues.en: I was wrong.
cues.zh: 我錯了。

cues.text: They thought I was kind of a dork.
cues.en: They thought I was kind of a dork.
cues.zh: 他們反而覺得我是個阿呆。

cues.text: They would use comic books as a way of distracting me.
cues.en: They would use comic books as a way of distracting me.
cues.zh: 他們會用漫畫來讓我分心。

cues.text: They would raise their hands and ask me questions like, “Mr. Yang, who do you think would win in a fight: Superman or the Hulk?”
cues.en: They would raise their hands and ask me questions like, “Mr. Yang, who do you think would win in a fight: Superman or the Hulk?”
cues.zh: 他們會舉手，問我像這樣的問題： 「楊老師，你認為如果超人 和浩克對打，誰會贏？」

cues.text: It seemed like my instincts in fifth grade were correct— comic books didn’t belong in the classroom—
cues.en: It seemed like my instincts in fifth grade were correct— comic books didn’t belong in the classroom—
cues.zh: 我在五年級時的直覺似乎是對的—— 漫畫不該出現在教室裡——

cues.text: but again I was wrong.
cues.en: but again I was wrong.
cues.zh: 但我又錯了。

cues.text: One semester I was asked to sub for this Algebra 2 class.
cues.en: One semester I was asked to sub for this Algebra 2 class.
cues.zh: 有一個學期，我去代 「代數二」這門課。

cues.text: But there was a problem.
cues.en: But there was a problem.
cues.zh: 但有個問題：每幾週， 我就有一、兩堂課非請假不可。

cues.text: Every couple of weeks, I had to miss 1 or 2 periods.
cues.en: Every couple of weeks, I had to miss 1 or 2 periods.
cues.zh: 但有個問題：每幾週， 我就有一、兩堂課非請假不可。

cues.text: In an effort to provide some sort of consistency for my students,
cues.en: In an effort to provide some sort of consistency for my students,
cues.zh: 為了提供我的學生 某種程度的一致性，

cues.text: I began videotaping myself giving lectures.
cues.en: I began videotaping myself giving lectures.
cues.zh: 我開始把自己教課的過程錄影下來。

cues.text: I tried to make these videos as engaging as possible.
cues.en: I tried to make these videos as engaging as possible.
cues.zh: 我盡量把這些影片做到能吸引人。

cues.text: These video lectures were a disaster.
cues.en: These video lectures were a disaster.
cues.zh: 這些課程影片簡直是災難， 有學生來找我，說像這樣的話：

cues.text: I had students coming up to me and saying things like, “Mr. Yang, we thought you were boring in person,
cues.en: I had students coming up to me and saying things like, “Mr. Yang, we thought you were boring in person,
cues.zh: 這些課程影片簡直是災難， 有學生來找我，說像這樣的話： 「楊老師，我們以為 你本人已經夠無趣了，但，

cues.text: but on video you are just unbearable.” So as a desperate second attempt, I began drawing these lectures as comics.
cues.en: but on video you are just unbearable.” So as a desperate second attempt, I began drawing these lectures as comics.
cues.zh: 影片中的你簡直讓人無法忍受。」 我做了絕望的第二次嘗試， 開始把這些課程畫成漫畫。

cues.text: Much to my surprise, these comics lectures were a hit.
cues.en: Much to my surprise, these comics lectures were a hit.
cues.zh: 出乎意料，這些課程漫畫大受歡迎。

cues.text: My students would ask me to make these for them, even when I could be there in person.
cues.en: My students would ask me to make these for them, even when I could be there in person.
cues.zh: 即使我可以親自教學，我的學生 還是希望我幫他們把課程畫成漫畫，

cues.text: it was like they liked cartoon me more than actual me.
cues.en: it was like they liked cartoon me more than actual me.
cues.zh: 好像他們比較喜歡漫畫版的我， 而不是真正的我。

cues.text: I began to understand the educational potential of comics.
cues.en: I began to understand the educational potential of comics.
cues.zh: 我開始瞭解漫畫的教育潛力。

cues.text: Comics lectures taught visually.
cues.en: Comics lectures taught visually.
cues.zh: 課程漫畫是用視覺的方式來教學。

cues.text: Our students grow up in a visual culture— so they’re used to taking in information that way.
cues.en: Our students grow up in a visual culture— so they’re used to taking in information that way.
cues.zh: 我們的學生是在視覺文化中長大， 所以他們很習慣 用視覺的方式吸收資訊。

cues.text: In a comic, past, present, and future all sit side by side on the same page.
cues.en: In a comic, past, present, and future all sit side by side on the same page.
cues.zh: 在漫畫中，過去，現在， 和未來都並存在同一頁上。

cues.text: This means that the rate of information flow is firmly in the hands of the reader.
cues.en: This means that the rate of information flow is firmly in the hands of the reader.
cues.zh: 意思就是，資訊流動的速度 完全由讀者掌控。

cues.text: When my students didn’t understand something in my comics lecture,
cues.en: When my students didn’t understand something in my comics lecture,
cues.zh: 當我的學生不瞭解 課程漫畫中的某部分時，

cues.text: they could just reread that passage as quickly or as slowly as they needed.
cues.en: they could just reread that passage as quickly or as slowly as they needed.
cues.zh: 當我的學生不瞭解 課程漫畫中的某部分時， 他們可以重讀那一段，閱讀速度 要快要慢完全根據自己的需求。

cues.text: Comic books first became a mass medium in the 1940s, with millions of copies selling every month.
cues.en: Comic books first became a mass medium in the 1940s, with millions of copies selling every month.
cues.zh: 在 1940 年代，漫畫 首次成為大眾媒介， 那時，每個月可以賣出數百萬冊。

cues.text: A lot of innovative teachers began bringing comics into their classrooms
cues.en: A lot of innovative teachers began bringing comics into their classrooms
cues.zh: 許多創新的老師開始 將漫畫帶進他們的教室，

cues.text: to experiment.
cues.en: to experiment.
cues.zh: 進行實驗。

cues.text: But then along comes this guy.
cues.en: But then along comes this guy.
cues.zh: 但後來這個傢伙出現了。

cues.text: This is child psychologist Dr. Fredrick Wortham, and in 1954, he wrote a book called “Seduction of the innocent,”
cues.en: This is child psychologist Dr. Fredrick Wortham, and in 1954, he wrote a book called “Seduction of the innocent,”
cues.zh: 他是兒童心理學家 佛雷德里克‧沃瑟姆博士， 在 1954 年，他寫了 《誘惑無辜者》這本書， 在書中，他主張漫畫 會造成青少年犯罪。

cues.text: where he argues that comic books cause juvenile delinquency.
cues.en: where he argues that comic books cause juvenile delinquency.
cues.zh: 在書中，他主張漫畫 會造成青少年犯罪。

cues.text: He was wrong.
cues.en: He was wrong.
cues.zh: 他錯了。

cues.text: In the 1940s and 50s, almost every kid in America read comic books.
cues.en: In the 1940s and 50s, almost every kid in America read comic books.
cues.zh: 在 1940 和 1950 年代，在美國 幾乎所有的孩子都會看漫畫。

cues.text: Dr. Wortham does a pretty dubious job of proving his case, but his book does inspire the Senate of the United States
cues.en: Dr. Wortham does a pretty dubious job of proving his case, but his book does inspire the Senate of the United States
cues.zh: 沃瑟姆博士並沒有為他的論點 提出可靠的證據， 但他的書確實導致美國參議院 舉行一系列聽證會， 以瞭解實際上漫畫是否會造成

cues.text: to hold a series of hearings to see if, in fact, comic books caused juvenile delinquency.
cues.en: to hold a series of hearings to see if, in fact, comic books caused juvenile delinquency.
cues.zh: 舉行一系列聽證會， 以瞭解實際上漫畫是否會造成 青少年犯罪。

cues.text: These hearings lasted for almost two months.
cues.en: These hearings lasted for almost two months.
cues.zh: 這些聽證會持續了近兩個月的時間，

cues.text: They ended inconclusively, but not before doing tremendous damage to the reputation of comic books
cues.en: They ended inconclusively, but not before doing tremendous damage to the reputation of comic books
cues.zh: 最後也沒得出結論， 但早就已經嚴重損毀了 美國大眾眼中漫畫的名聲。

cues.text: in the eyes of the American public.
cues.en: in the eyes of the American public.
cues.zh: 美國大眾眼中漫畫的名聲。

cues.text: It wasn’t until the 1970s that a few brave souls started making their way back in
cues.en: It wasn’t until the 1970s that a few brave souls started making their way back in
cues.zh: 一直到 1970 年代，才有幾個 勇敢的人重新涉足這個領域，

cues.text: and it really wasn’t until pretty recently— maybe the last decade or so—
cues.en: and it really wasn’t until pretty recently— maybe the last decade or so—
cues.zh: 且要到非常近期—— 也許是過去十年左右——

cues.text: that comics have seen more widespread acceptance among American educators.
cues.en: that comics have seen more widespread acceptance among American educators.
cues.zh: 美國的教育界才比較廣泛接受漫畫。

cues.text: And this is even happening at Bishop O’Dowd, where I used to teach.
cues.en: And this is even happening at Bishop O’Dowd, where I used to teach.
cues.zh: 甚至連我以前任職的 奧多德主教高中都開始接受了。

cues.text: Mr. Smith, one of my former colleagues, uses Scott McCloud’s “Understanding Comics” in his literature and film class.
cues.en: Mr. Smith, one of my former colleagues, uses Scott McCloud’s “Understanding Comics” in his literature and film class.
cues.zh: 甚至連我以前任職的 奧多德主教高中都開始接受了。 我的前同事史密斯老師把史考特‧ 麥克勞德的《漫畫原來要這樣看》 用在他的「文學與電影」課。

cues.text: Mr. Burns assigns a comics essay to his students every year
cues.en: Mr. Burns assigns a comics essay to his students every year
cues.zh: 伯恩斯老師每年都會要求 他的學生繳交一篇漫畫論文，

cues.text: by asking his students to process a prose novel using images.
cues.en: by asking his students to process a prose novel using images.
cues.zh: 做法是要求學生用影象來呈現 一部散文小說的內容。

cues.text: And Miss Murac uses my own “American Born Chinese” with her English one students.
cues.en: And Miss Murac uses my own “American Born Chinese” with her English one students.
cues.zh: 穆拉克老師則是用我寫的 《生在美國的中國人》 來教「英文一」的學生。

cues.text: Over in the library, Miss Counts has built a pretty impressive graphic novel collection
cues.en: Over in the library, Miss Counts has built a pretty impressive graphic novel collection
cues.zh: 在圖書館，伯特小姐為奧多德 主教高中建立了精采的漫畫館藏。

cues.text: for Bishop O’Dowd.
cues.en: for Bishop O’Dowd.
cues.zh: 在圖書館，伯特小姐為奧多德 主教高中建立了精采的漫畫館藏。

cues.text: A school library journal article stated that the mere presence of graphic novels
cues.en: A school library journal article stated that the mere presence of graphic novels
cues.zh: 有一篇學校圖書館期刊文章 指出光是在圖書館內納入漫畫館藏

cues.text: in a library increased usage by about 80%, and increased the circulation of non-comics material by about 30%.
cues.en: in a library increased usage by about 80%, and increased the circulation of non-comics material by about 30%.
cues.zh: 指出光是在圖書館內納入漫畫館藏 就能讓圖書館的使用量增加約八成， 並讓非漫畫館藏的流通量 增加了約三成。

cues.text: American cartoonists are now producing more explicitly educational content
cues.en: American cartoonists are now producing more explicitly educational content
cues.zh: 美國漫畫家現在 為幼稚園到十二年級市場 創作的明確教育內容 比以往都還要多。

cues.text: for the K-12 market than ever before.
cues.en: for the K-12 market than ever before.
cues.zh: 創作的明確教育內容 比以往都還要多。

cues.text: More comics and graphic novels are starting to tackle math and science topics.
cues.en: More comics and graphic novels are starting to tackle math and science topics.
cues.zh: 有越來越多漫畫開始 處理數學和科學主題。

cues.text: STEM comics and graphic novels really are like this uncharted territory
cues.en: STEM comics and graphic novels really are like this uncharted territory
cues.zh: 科學、科技、工程、數學漫畫就像是 等待著被探索的未知領土。

cues.text: ready to be explored.
cues.en: ready to be explored.
cues.zh: 等待著被探索的未知領土。

cues.text: America is finally waking up to the fact that comic books
cues.en: America is finally waking up to the fact that comic books
cues.zh: 美國終於認清了這個事實： 漫畫確實應該成為 教育工作者的工具之一。

cues.text: really do belong in every educator’s toolkit.
cues.en: really do belong in every educator’s toolkit.
cues.zh: 漫畫確實應該成為 教育工作者的工具之一。

cues.text: The educational potential is there just waiting to be tapped
cues.en: The educational potential is there just waiting to be tapped
cues.zh: 教育潛力就在那裡， 等著像你這樣有創意的人去善用。

cues.text: by creative people like you.
cues.en: by creative people like you.
cues.zh: 等著像你這樣有創意的人去善用。
